name: dual-clock
title: Dual Clock
description: Two world clocks side by side, one light and one dark, their hands running on the UI thread.

perf.budget: Hands are views on continuous UI-thread timings, so the clocks animate at rest with no re-render. One timer per minute keeps the spoken time current.

a11y.reducedMotion: The second hand is removed and the other hands move once a minute.
a11y.screenReader: One label with both times ("TYO 21:04, RIO 09:04").

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { DualClock } from '@/components/kinetik/dual-clock';

<DualClock
  zones={[
    { code: 'TYO', offset: 9, face: 'day' },
    { code: 'RIO', offset: -3, face: 'night' },
  ]}
/>;
```

## When to use

- Teams and travellers who watch two time zones.
- A clock widget on a dashboard.

## When not to use

- More than two zones. Use a list.
- Places with daylight saving, unless you update `offset` yourself.

## Notes

- `offset` is hours from UTC, so daylight saving is yours to handle.
- Pass `time` to show a fixed moment. The clocks then hold still.
- Each face follows the hour unless you set `face`.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add dual-clock`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
